From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@acmecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: Acme - Redwood bakeoff: discovery recap & next steps

Hi Jane / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — really productive conversation. As promised, a quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we scope the bake-off.

High-level pain points you shared
- Production latency spikes on peak traffic causing timeouts for chat experiences (~95th pct > 1.2s token-to-token).
- High per-request cost from current cloud endpoints when handling large multi-turn contexts.
- Cache/kv reuse is inconsistent across services; engineering team wants predictable per-session throughput.

Current stack
- Inference: mix of cloud endpoints (managed) + experiments on vLLM for on-prem prototypes.
- Orchestration: homegrown request router + Redis-based session store.
- SLOs: < 200ms p50, <600ms p95 for short-chat flows; heavier batch workloads tolerate higher latency.

Success criteria for the bake-off (draft — please edit if I missed anything)
- Latency: p95 token-to-token <= 700ms for 8K context, avg throughput >= 20 tok/s per GPU for the benchmark workload.
- Cost: target < 60% of current cloud endpoint spend for same request profile (we'll exchange numbers in NDA channel).
- Functional/quality: no regressions on your critical prompt set (we'll run the 50-check eval you mentioned).
- Operational: seamless routing/fallback and a reproducible benchmark harness you can run internally.

Benchmarks / data we will run
- vLLM baseline (your current on-prem runs)
- TGI-based run (if you want to include as a comparative open runtime)
- Redwood hosted and dedicated configurations (quantized variants if you want to test those)

Attachments included
- redwood-bakeoff-harness.zip — minimal harness + sample load profile and instructions
- acme-acceptance-criteria.xlsx — draft acceptance criteria (please fill out numbers where you have them)

Proposed next steps
1) Confirm acceptance criteria spreadsheet and any additional test prompts (you fill; we can redact PII).
2) Schedule technical kickoff with your infra/ML eng (Rishi and Dev from our side will join).
3) Redwood to provision a 2-week bake-off plan (we typically run a 10–14 day window to capture steady-state).
4) Decide on baselines: please confirm if you want both vLLM and TGI included.

Can you confirm the acceptance targets and availability for a technical kickoff next week?

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear recap — this matches our notes. A few quick clarifications / asks:

I'll add our ML infra lead (Tom) to the kickoff invite. Procurement copied here for NDA/PO flow — they may request a short SOW.

Available for a technical kickoff on Thu 02/19 at 16:00 UTC or Fri 02/20 morning PT — let us know which works.

- Redwood configurations: hosted standard, hosted quantized, dedicated (reserved pool) with 1–2x burst capacity.
- Workloads: short-chat p95 target (they asked to tighten to 600ms), multi-turn session throughput, and cold-start behavior for long contexts.

Tech asks for the team
- Rishi: can you sketch the benchmark harness mapping (how we’ll hook into their load profile + the eval set)? I sent the harness ZIP in the thread.
- Dev: please prepare a vLLM runbook we can hand to Acme (docker + sample config) and a TGI run that matches our measurement conventions.
- Also we should prepare cost-per-1M-token estimates for each config (hosted vs. dedicated vs. vLLM on their infra) — high-level ballpark OK for kickoff.

Schedule
- Proposed kickoff Thu 2026-02-19 16:00 UTC (Jane said this works). I'll create the calendar invite and include you both.

Let me know if any of the asks are unrealistic for the first week — we can phase some items into the second week.

Thanks,
